## Market Position for BTC

Bitcoin trades at $79,731 with a market [cap](/cap-4) of $1.59T and 24h volume of $33.36B. The latest ranked market snapshot places BTC at #1 by market capitalization. The token is -36.76% from its all-time high of $126,080, recorded on October 6, 2025. Its all-time low is $67.81, recorded on July 6, 2013, while the 30-day move is +10.45%. Circulating supply is 20,028,850, total supply is 20,028,850, and max supply is 21,000,000. Bitcoin has a recorded genesis date of January 3, 2009. The volume-to-market-[cap](/cap-4) ratio is 2.09%, which helps separate active markets from thin markets. A higher ratio usually means recent trading activity is easier to observe, while a very low ratio can make price changes less reliable as a signal.

## Supply and Valuation

Circulating supply is 20,028,850, total supply is 20,028,850, and max supply is 21,000,000. Fully diluted valuation is $1.59T. Market [cap](/cap-4) and FDV can diverge when a large portion of supply is not circulating, so investors should compare circulating supply, total supply, and unlock or emission information before relying on valuation multiples.

## What Could Change the Setup

Bitcoin would need stronger evidence across volume, liquidity, development activity, and category momentum for the setup to improve. Weak follow-through, falling volume, large unlocks, contract migrations, or negative security events would weaken the research case even if the spot price rises for a short period.

## FAQ

**What is Bitcoin?**

Bitcoin is the world's first decentralized cryptocurrency, created in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto.

**Is BTC a low-risk asset?**

No crypto asset should be treated as low risk by default. TokenRadar currently shows a risk score of 4/10, and that score should be checked against volatility, liquidity, supply, and recent events.

**What market data matters most for BTC?**

The most useful starting points are price, market [cap](/cap-4), 24h volume, market rank, ATH distance, circulating supply, and the 30-day trend.

**Does this overview recommend buying Bitcoin?**

No. It is a structured research summary for comparing data points and risks.

## Continue Research

Use this BTC overview as the starting point, then open the [price scenario page](/bitcoin/price-prediction) for upside, base, and downside conditions or the [buying checklist](/bitcoin/how-to-buy) for venue, fee, custody, and network verification. To compare Bitcoin with broader research concepts, review [market cap basics](/learn/market-cap-explained), [FDV and dilution](/learn/fully-diluted-valuation-fdv), and [liquidity depth](/learn/liquidity-depth). Moving through those pages gives the market snapshot a clearer decision framework without turning this article into a buy or sell recommendation.

For BTC research, the important control is consistency between the live market snapshot and the longer historical record. A single 24h move can be noisy, while market [cap](/cap-4) rank, 30-day performance, all-time high distance, supply structure, and volume-to-[cap](/cap-4) ratio create a more durable comparison set. This is why the article separates market data from decision rules and keeps the conclusion conditional.

Bitcoin also needs category-aware interpretation. A Smart Contract Platform token with high liquidity can behave very differently from a low-volume asset with the same percentage move. The practical question is whether volume, spread quality, supply data, and catalyst evidence confirm the move or contradict it.

The safest way to use this overview article is as a checklist. Confirm the latest price, check the current rank, compare 24h volume with market [cap](/cap-4), review the ATH and ATL dates, and look for any project-specific changes before treating the data as current enough for research.
